cells.tense: You are sitting with someone now and still keep your own edges.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: This week, sit with someone in something heavy and hold your own shape. Stay when you would normally start fixing, and when their weight starts to feel like yours, come back to your own two feet.
cells.core:
You can feel what another person is going through and still know where you stop. That is the working version, and it holds because nothing gets rushed — no fixing, no folding in. You read a person quickly, what they need and what to leave alone, well before you could explain how you know. That reading is what makes the whole thing land.

Someone close is carrying something heavy. Sit with them in it and keep your own shape while you do. Stay longer than usual. The pull to take it on will show up; let it pass through without acting on it. What you learn from staying is the difference between being with someone and going under with them.

cells.tense: Soon you will not be able to say whose feeling this is.
cells.act: let the thing end that is already over
cells.ask: What you are still carrying for someone is already finished. Let it end — close it once, in the plainest way — and then leave it closed this week.
cells.core:
You feel everything, and lately there is no gap left. What someone else is going through arrives in you as your own, and you carry it all day without being asked. It reads as care from inside your own head. From outside it looks like you have stopped knowing which feelings started with you.

Something you are carrying for someone is already over. Let it end. Not with a ceremony — with a plain act that closes it, once. Then leave it closed. No checking back, no reopening to see if it held. When an ending is allowed to be an ending, the weight comes off, and you find out which of those feelings were ever yours.

cells.tense: You were there, and you have been standing outside it since.
cells.act: adjust one dial a little, then stop
cells.ask: In one conversation, turn a single dial — a question where you would comment, a pause you would fill — then stop adjusting and see what comes through.
cells.core:
You know what to attend to. You can walk into a room and sense what matters before anyone has said much, and that has not gone anywhere. What has gone is the feeling arriving with it. Conversations stay polite and finished because you have stopped expecting anything from them, and no one notices, because you are still good at this.

One adjustment is the whole of it. In a single conversation, shift something small — ask instead of comment, let a silence run longer than is comfortable, say the accurate sentence where you would say the easy one. Then stop, and do not keep tuning. You are not trying to manufacture a feeling. You are giving one real thing room to come through a door you left open.

cells.tense: You are already giving something you do not count as giving.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Bring up the last three times someone came to you. Look for the move that repeats — what you did, and when. Put it in one sentence, and change nothing yet.
cells.core:
You keep showing up for people in a way they feel and you do not. You will sit with someone for an hour, remember the detail they mentioned weeks ago, know when to stop talking. Ask about it and you would say you were simply there, nothing special. The receiving end reads it differently, and has for a while.

Take the last three times someone brought you something. Do not grade them. Look for the shape that repeats: what you did each time, and at which moment. Put it in one sentence. Nothing changes yet. Seeing the move is the entire ask, and it is how something you already do starts registering as yours.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: 'others feel your compassion' — the record carries it, but I have no evidence for any particular person in the room, so I keep it as others' experience generally and never as fact about them. Reader's likely objection: in the Unacknowledged cell they may say 'I don't feel indifferent, I feel nothing because there's nothing to feel' — the ask survives that because tracing the pattern is useful whether or not the reading is right. Sentence that serves me more than them: 'the people who lean on you feel the floor hold' — cut, no floor metaphor; say it plain.
